source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) -- Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company reported ending FY25 virtually debt-free with ~INR 1,471 crore in cash and INR 2,726 crore in liquid assets (broker/press coverage), implying minimal floating-rate liability exposure, though no explicit % was disclosed.

pli_scheme.evidence: Emcure Pharma was approved under Group B of the government's PLI Scheme for Pharmaceuticals, alongside Biocon, MSN Labs, Wockhardt, Alembic Pharma, Macleods Pharma, Biological E, Natco Pharma and Strides Pharma Science (government/news coverage; no revenue % disclosed).

rural.evidence: Coverage notes Radico's value/mass brands (e.g., 8PM) have deep strength in semi-urban and rural segments via extensive distribution, but no revenue % was disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: News coverage states 'surging crude oil prices and a weaker rupee are increasing import costs for packaging and other inputs' (glass bottles, PET); no exact raw-material % disclosed.

rural.evidence: Officer's Choice Whisky (mass-premium, India's top exported spirits brand) is distributed through 79,000+ outlets and is described as a preferred choice in rural and semi-urban markets; no revenue % disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Reporting on ABD notes crude-linked packaging inputs (PET, glass bottles) rose 20-25% and packaging resins 30-50% amid crude oil price spikes, and that 'packaging materials represent approximately 30% of ABD's total manufacturing cost.'

inr_exposure.evidence: Company description: 'care enablement platform assisting physician enterprises in the US, Canada and Australia, with a focus on the US markets' -- no explicit revenue % or hedging disclosure found in accessible sources.

china_plus_one.evidence: FY2024-25 Annual Report: 'Diversification has been our way of building resilience and discovering new growth. By expanding across products, platforms, and geographies, we are reducing concentration risks while creating new opportunities in emerging mobility ecosystems.' No explicit 'China+1' framing tying FY24-25 revenue growth directly to customers diversifying away from China (that framing appeared more explicitly in later FY26 commentary re: supply-chain diversification away from China and distressed European driveline suppliers).

pli_scheme.evidence: Sona Comstar became the first automotive component supplier certified under India's Auto PLI scheme (traction motors for EV two/three-wheelers); management noted PLI income had roughly a 1.9pp positive effect on EBITDA margin in FY25, but no revenue % was disclosed.

rural.evidence: 'Large part of supply is coming in tier 2/3 towns in the coming years... supply growth in top 8 cities expected to be 5% and key leisure markets ~10%' -- tier 2/3 expansion narrative present but no rural revenue % disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Consolidated long-term borrowings Rs 224.70 cr (FY25) vs Rs 260.49 cr (FY24), short-term borrowings nil; 'major portion of outstanding debt are lease liabilities'; interest coverage ratio 13.34x; near net-cash position suggests low rate sensitivity but no floating-rate % disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: International Patient Services revenue contributed ~6% of total revenue in FY24/FY25 (Q4FY25: Rs 55.7 cr, +17% YoY) -- closest disclosed 'foreign revenue' proxy; not stated as USD-specific with a hedging policy.

china_plus_one.evidence: 'Exports accounted for approximately 74% of net sales in FY25, compared to 56% in FY24.' Revenue mix described as balanced between emerging markets (50%) and regulated markets (40%, US/EU/Japan) across 27+ countries; company 'sourced 71% of materials domestically and now manufactures over 90% of its products' (backward integration reducing import/China dependency). No single quote explicitly frames this as customer-driven 'China+1' diversification, so scored moderate.

pli_scheme.evidence: Not applicable to the FY2024-25 report period. In Jan 2026 the company (post name-change from Ami Organics to Acutaas Chemicals) received Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS) approval -- a different, newer scheme, not classic PLI -- for an electrolyte-additives project. This postdates FY24-25 and was not in the FY24-25 AR MD&A.

rural.evidence: Government focus on 100% electrification of existing railway networks, rural electrification schemes, and Bharat Net optical fibre rollout expected to drive rural/semi-urban cable demand (no revenue % disclosed).

govt_capex.evidence: Key growth drivers include increased government investment in roads, railways and housing, plus rural electrification/power distribution infra; power sector's Rs 3.12 lakh crore capex plan generates cable demand across transmission, substations, rural electrification and renewable projects (no specific revenue % from government projects disclosed).

rate_sensitive.evidence: Total debt ~Rs 185.8M with a debt-to-equity ratio of ~0.4%, i.e. minimal leverage; finance costs fell 17.7% YoY in FY25 (no floating vs fixed breakdown found).

crude_exposure.evidence: Copper is ~70% of raw material cost for electrical wiring (not crude-linked); PVC (a crude/ethylene derivative) is also a key input and price hikes of up to 3% were announced to offset raw-material cost inflation; no combined crude-linked raw material % disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports are a small part of the business (e.g. ~Rs 50cr in a recent quarter vs ~Rs 1,900cr quarterly revenue); management noted a revamped export team but no USD revenue % or hedging policy found.

china_plus_one.evidence: "Rising preference for Indian fluorochemical suppliers amid China+1 sentiment benefits Navin Fluorine's export-led business" -- third-party/analyst commentary, not a direct quote sourced from the AR MD&A itself; CDMO/export mix specifics were described as 'not materially different from historical levels' by management on an earnings call rather than tied explicitly to China+1 in disclosed text.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Total debt ~Rs 14.7B, debt-to-equity ratio ~55.9%, interest coverage ~5.8x (moderate leverage; no floating-rate % disclosed).

crude_exposure.evidence: Gross margins saw a sequential dip due to higher raw material costs and a lag in passing through price increases; no explicit crude-oil-linked raw material % found.

inr_exposure.evidence: CDMO business described as having a 'strong export bias'; HFC R32 exports ramped to ~3,300 MTPA in H1FY25; no USD revenue % or hedging policy disclosed in sources reviewed.

pli_scheme.evidence: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilisers was still working toward implementing a PLI scheme for the specialty chemicals sector; no confirmation found that NFIL is a current PLI beneficiary.

rural.evidence: FY25 focus described as distribution expansion (1 lakh+ unique outlets billed, direct distributor contribution up from 38% in FY24 to 71% in Q4FY25); no rural-vs-urban revenue split disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Debt-to-equity ratio ~0.09, i.e. low leverage (no floating-rate breakdown found).

crude_exposure.evidence: Third-party commentary: most plastic packaging (polyethylene/polypropylene) is crude-oil derived, and packaging is ~15-20% of typical FMCG cost; one source estimated ~10-15% cost exposure for some Honasa brand formulations to crude/palm-oil-linked inputs -- not sourced from the AR itself.

inr_exposure.evidence: International presence (UAE, Qatar, Nepal, Malaysia, Maldives, Mauritius, mostly via Amazon) but stated India remains its primary focal market in the medium term; no export/USD revenue % disclosed.

govt_capex.evidence: Strategic focus on 'operational efficiency, integrated manufacturing, and infrastructure-driven demand,' deepening presence in 'defence, engineering, railways, infrastructure and real estate'; no specific % of revenue from government projects disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company described as 'almost debt free' with debt-to-equity ~0.0 in FY24; a large new capex program (Rs 2,700cr+) was subsequently approved, which may change the debt profile going forward.

inr_exposure.evidence: Company exports to 30-40+ countries; export contribution reported inconsistently across sources/years (~16% in 2022, ~21% of FY26 revenue, ~10.6% of FY26 turnover per another source) -- no figure could be confidently attributed to FY2024-25 specifically, so left null.

pli_scheme.evidence: "Shyam Metalics Flat Products has been selected to make investments under the production-linked incentive (PLI) programme for specialty steel, along with other companies like Gallant Metalliks and Sunflag Iron and Steel."

china_plus_one.evidence: Management noted conversion of RFQs into pilot projects/contracts amid global clients diversifying supply chains away from China; industry commentary noted large-scale financial gains from this shift would take '3-5 years' -- narrative present and tied to order/pipeline activity, but not yet clearly attributed to realized FY24-25 revenue growth.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company in a net cash position of approximately -Rs 7,427 crore (cash exceeds debt) as of March 2025, i.e. very low reliance on borrowings/interest-rate sensitivity.

crude_exposure.evidence: Raw material costs, particularly solvents, 'doubled or tripled in price' amid Middle East geopolitical tension; rising crude oil/energy prices increase the cost of petrochemical-based raw materials essential for APIs -- no specific % of raw material cost quantified.

inr_exposure.evidence: ~89% of FY25 revenue was export-derived (Europe ~56%, North America ~16% of total revenue); a net forex loss of Rs 7cr was reported in a subsequent quarter (Q1 FY27) vs a Rs 39cr gain a year earlier, indicating real forex exposure, but no formal hedging policy or USD-specific revenue % was found.

pli_scheme.evidence: No confirmation found that Divi's Laboratories is a beneficiary of the bulk-drugs/API PLI scheme in the sources reviewed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Press coverage of LG India's export strategy: 'LG India Expands Export Strategy, Eyes 50-Market Manufacturing Footprint'; exports grew ~30% YoY in a recent quarter; company targets a double-digit share of revenue from exports, supported by expanded domestic manufacturing (new Sri City, Andhra Pradesh facility) -- third-party commentary frames this as China+1 supply-chain diversification, but this framing was not confirmed as the company's own explicit AR language.

rural.evidence: 'Tier 2 and 3 cities and rural areas are increasingly buying consumer electronics, thanks to better awareness and availability'; LG's India-exclusive 'Essential Series' appliances positioned for India's expanding middle class including rural/semi-urban buyers; no revenue % disclosed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Reported to be shifting from short-tenor (3-6 month) forward contracts to longer-duration hedges, and increasing local sourcing by 3-4 percentage points in FY26 to reduce structural forex exposure.
inr_exposure.evidence: 'LG India, along with broader India Inc, is shifting from short-tenor (3-6 month) forward contracts to longer-duration covers... increasing its local sourcing by 3-4 percentage points in FY26.'

pli_scheme.evidence: Could not confirm LG Electronics India's participation in the Large-Scale Electronics Manufacturing PLI (which primarily targets mobile phones/components); LG India's core products are appliances/TVs/air solutions, not the scheme's named target segments in available sources.

china_plus_one.evidence: Company operates in 50+ countries with subsidiaries/distribution in UK, Netherlands, Thailand, US, Singapore, positioned as a 'one-stop solution' global wire rope supplier -- export presence well established but no explicit China+1/diversification framing tied to revenue growth was found.

govt_capex.evidence: 'Energy, roads, urban, and railways together account for ~71% of projected investment under India's National Infrastructure Pipeline'; Usha Martin produces locked-coil wire ropes and stay cable strands for high-speed rail and bridge projects, and serves clients including Coal India, ONGC and Indian Railways -- narrative strongly government-capex-linked but no specific revenue % disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company reported 'entirely debt-free at the standalone level' with a net cash position (~Rs 111 crore) funding capex (Rs 300-350 crore/year) from internal accruals -- implying low floating-rate liability exposure, but no specific % disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Primary raw material is wire rod steel, not crude oil directly; one source notes 'demand for wire ropes improved after crude oil prices went up' (demand-side linkage via oil & offshore/wind applications), not a raw-material cost linkage.

inr_exposure.evidence: 'International revenue constitutes 57% of total revenue' / 'international markets accounted for 55% of total revenues in FY25' -- figures from secondary sources vary slightly (55-57%).

rate_sensitive.evidence: Consolidated non-current borrowings reported around Rs 4,704 crore with average cost of borrowing cited near 8.4-8.65%; sources note the company 'maintains both floating and fixed rate borrowings' but no split % was found.

china_plus_one.evidence: 'APL Apollo Steel Tubes exports to 20 countries worldwide' -- export presence confirmed but no explicit China+1/supply-chain diversification narrative tied to revenue growth found; company described as 'India's largest producer of Structural steel tubes' focused primarily on domestic demand.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Analyst notes mention 'slight buildup in debt' in H1 with a target of reaching net-cash position by FY25 end as operating cash flows normalize; no floating-rate % disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Primary raw material is HRC (Hot Rolled Coil) steel, not crude oil. 'The company is susceptible to margin movements in steel HRC prices given the high raw material intensity...volatility in HRC prices can directly compress margins.' Management reportedly passes through HRC price changes within 5-8 days. This is a steel/commodity exposure, not a direct crude-oil linkage.

pli_scheme.evidence: A PLI Scheme for Specialty Steel exists (Rs 6,322 crore outlay, FY23-24 to FY27-28) and analyst commentary speculates APL Apollo 'could benefit' given its capacity expansion (2.6 MT to 4 MT by FY25), but no confirmed approved-beneficiary status or revenue % was found.

china_plus_one.evidence: Belrise serves 29 global OEMs (incl. Bajaj Auto, Honda, Tata Motors, Jaguar Land Rover) across US, Japan, UK, China; secondary commentary states its 'broad and diversified customer base... positions it well for growth as global automotive supply chains become more integrated and as foreign OEMs continue to invest in India.' Company also completed a European aerospace acquisition (SDM) to diversify into high-precision aerospace manufacturing. Diversification/export-momentum narrative present but not explicitly framed as 'China+1' in sourced material.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Net debt reported to have fallen from ~Rs 2,607 crore (Mar-2025) to ~Rs 961 crore (Sep-2025); no floating-rate % disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: RHP-derived risk-factor language: 'As an international operator with export activities, Belrise is exposed to currency exchange rate fluctuations, particularly between the Indian Rupee against the USD and Euro.'

pli_scheme.evidence: A PLI Scheme for Automobile and Auto Components exists (Rs 25,938 crore outlay, FY22-23 to FY26-27, 115 companies applied); Belrise's specific approved-beneficiary status and any revenue % was not confirmed in available sources.
